lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The frozen macOS baseline and the first focused fix both failed the exact-evidence boundary: the Quick Panel consequence review showed the new reviewed sentence, but the decision step could still freeze an older already-reviewed sentence. That was a real evidence-state mixing veto on the frozen artifact. The later source-bound v2 retest cleared the same path in real UI and AX evidence: unconfirmed current source disabled save, selected-but-unconfirmed still disabled save, confirmed current source enabled save, the decision step showed only the current exact evidence, and the receipt still stated that nothing was sent.
findings.evidence: Baseline mismatch: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/screenshots/11-new-selection-analysis.png, docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/screenshots/12-context-decision-return.png, and docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/logs/retest-decision-ax.txt. First fix still falling back to older evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/screenshots/retest-01-new-selection-analysis.png, docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/screenshots/retest-02-decision-exact-evidence.png, docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/logs/retest-pre-submit-ax.txt, and docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/macos/logs/retest-decision-ax.txt. findings.user_impact: On the frozen baseline, a recruiter could believe they were approving the currently visible source while the saved decision was still grounded in an older reviewed sentence.
findings.recommendation: Treat the source-bound v2 behavior as the minimum acceptable safety floor. Save eligibility must remain bound to the current reviewed source item, never to an older eligible fallback item that survives from a prior receipt.
findings.verification: Repeat the five-step retest on the current build: current source unconfirmed keeps save disabled; selecting Candidate without confirming still keeps save disabled; confirming that exact source enables save; the decision step contains only the current exact evidence and excludes the older sentence; the resulting receipt says that nothing was sent.

findings.observation: The current post-change Web behavior is materially more truthful under backend loss: local logout no longer waits indefinitely for backend logout, Lab settles from a connecting state to an explicit unavailable state instead of implying progress, and the frozen TS-ID boundary case now presents a coherent no-action/clarification state. Those are real safety improvements, but they do not establish release proof because the canonical backend loop and integrated iOS governed loop were not run on September 3, 2026.
findings.evidence: Logout deadline and local completion: apps/web/app/login/actions.ts defines BACKEND_LOGOUT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_500 and uses logoutBackendWithinDeadline(), while apps/web/lib/workspaceShell.test.ts asserts that an unreachable backend must not block local sign-out; the resulting signed-out surface is retained in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/45-logout-post-change-home.png. Lab truthful failure: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/16-workspace-lab-backend-unavailable-desktop.png shows the prior connecting state, and docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/43-workspace-lab-post-change-retest-desktop.png shows the settled unavailable state with no test-state creation claim. TS-ID boundary coherence: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/44-boundary-identity-post-change-retest.png. Deterministic release proof remains withheld in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/checks/v1-p0-runtime.json where agent_live_release_claim is missing_proof and in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/checks/run-summary.md where all 12 release gates remain needs_review. The iOS lane explicitly records the canonical backend as unavailable in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/ios/ios-run-summary.md.
findings.user_impact: The product now fails more honestly instead of hiding behind stale state or endless loading, but that still does not prove safe account-bound write approval, readback, retry reconciliation, or integrated native behavior.
findings.recommendation: Do not grant release pass from this review packet. Require one canonical backend rerun and one integrated iOS governed loop with explicit identity binding, approved write or truthful no-write receipt, retry/reconciliation behavior, and destination readback evidence.
findings.verification: Run a healthy canonical backend for Today, People, Evals, and Lab, then execute at least one governed approval path through readback. Separately run the same governed loop on iOS with integrated receipt/readback evidence instead of simulator-only or deterministic proofs.

strengths: Post-change disconnected workspace behavior is safer and more truthful: the account-scoped Today routes now say that governed state is unavailable instead of substituting cached or test state, as shown in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/13-workspace-today-backend-unavailable-desktop.png and docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/28-workspace-today-backend-unavailable-narrow.png.

Logout now preserves the local account boundary even when the backend hangs: code enforces a 1.5 second backend deadline before local sign-out continues, and the resulting signed-out public surface is visible in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/45-logout-post-change-home.png.

Lab no longer presents an endless or misleading connected state during backend loss: the route settles to an explicit unavailable state with retry and return paths, shown in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/web/screenshots/43-workspace-lab-post-change-retest-desktop.png.

Deterministic safety coverage remains strong and source-bound without over-claiming release: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/checks/eval-p0-artifacts/runs/evaluation_run_11a177dd48f38d887c72ef9f9d99a8e3/run-artifact.dab680ee2f2aa882f9e76d6b4cee0af3dea2d20f8a2e897726d7afb567d9e4bf.json records TS-ID-103 passes for identity, source-bound observation, memory provenance, and terminal truthfulness, while docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/checks/v1-p0-runtime.json still truthfully marks live release proof as missing.
missing_evidence: No live canonical backend run in this lane proved account-scoped identity binding, approved write, destination readback, duplicate/retry reconciliation, permission revocation, or deletion against the governed backend.

No integrated iOS governed loop against the canonical backend was captured on September 3, 2026; docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-system-e2e-agent-review/ios/ios-run-summary.md explicitly records the canonical backend as unavailable, and VoiceOver plus real destination write paths remain not run.

The frozen baseline commit 5ba505ae45e3df51b3339427da79c96fde42c137 cannot be granted release pass from this lens because its macOS exact-evidence veto was only resolved on the later source-bound v2 retest build, not on the frozen artifact itself.
open_questions: Which exact local or shared backend environment should own the canonical governed rerun without colliding with the already-reserved localhost and Docker resources?
Should release adjudication explicitly fail the frozen baseline commit while separately accepting the source-bound v2 retest as the new minimum safety floor for future candidates?
